v: Therefore, holy brothers, who share in the heavenly calling, set your focus on Jesus, the apostle and high priest whom we confess.
Therefore, holy brothers, sharers of a heavenly calling, consider carefully the apostle and high priest of our confession, Jesus,

My fellow believers, God has set you apart for himself, and he has summoned us together from heaven. Since {I have told you what Jesus has done,} you should think about him. God sent him to us, and he is the ruling priest in whom we say we believe.
God has set you apart for himself
He was faithful to the One who appointed Him, just as Moses was faithful in all God’s house.

He faithfully served God, who made him {a ruling priest}. {He is} like Moses, who also {faithfully served God} as part of God’s people.
For Jesus has been counted worthy of greater glory than Moses, just as the builder of a house has greater honor than the house itself.
For this one has been considered worthy of greater glory than Moses, according to how much greater honor the one building it has {than} the house.

Now each building has a builder who made it, and people rightly praise the builder more than {they praise} the building. Similarly, God is the builder who made everything. Therefore, people should praise Jesus{, who is God,} more than {they praise} Moses{, whom God made}. \*
And every house is built by someone, but God is the builder of everything.
For every house is built by someone, but God {is} the one having built all things. \*
Now Moses was faithful as a servant in all God’s house, testifying to what would be spoken later.
And Moses {was} indeed faithful as a servant in his entire house, for a testimony of the {things that} would be spoken in the future;
Moses faithfully served God as one who helped all God’s people. In that way, he already proclaimed what God says now {about Jesus}.
